title: KV eviction escrow protocol and simulated failure injection
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a deterministic, auditable eviction handshake that prevents prefix-corruption during continuous batching and aggressive prefetching. This ticket proposes an "eviction escrow" protocol: evictors obtain a short-lived escrow token for candidate KV slices, coordinate with in-flight batch owners, and only commit reclamation once a set of lightweight invariants are proven. The protocol aims to maintain correctness across LRU/TTL/prefix-aware heuristics while enabling GPU slab reclamation and cooperative prefetching.

Motivation:
- Continuous batching and aggressive prefetch reduce GPU stall and improve throughput, but they increase races between eviction and inflight cache readers/writers.
- Existing heuristics (LRU + TTL) work well for steady state but are brittle under bursty prefix-heavy workloads and when batches hold references across kernel boundaries.
- We need a pragmatic protocol that: (1) protects prefix-affinity invariants, (2) allows bounded-time reclamation for GPU memory pressure, and (3) is testable via fault injection and property tests.

Proposal (high level):
1) Escrow token allocation: evictor marks a slice with an escrow token containing: token_id, proposed-evict-level (soft/hard), epoch, and hint-set of prefixes touched. Token is visible to batch owners via a small in-memory ledger.
2) Inflight check window: batch owners periodically check the ledger; if they hold references to a tokened slice they register a short lease (ms-resolution) indicating active use.
3) Quiesce-or-renegotiate: evictor waits up to a configurable grace window (default 50ms) for active leases to either expire or for owners to signal a safe demote path (e.g., copy-to-evict-buffer or move to colder memory).
4) Commit with proof: when grace window elapses with no active leases, evictor commits eviction and emits a compact proof record (token_id, epoch, commit-timestamp, affected-prefixes) appended to eviction-audit log for later replay or verification.
5) Fallbacks: if grace window exceeds a threshold or owner signals inability to demote, evictor either (a) lower reclaim aggressiveness (downgrade to soft) or (b) defer eviction to next pass.

Correctness invariants to guarantee:
- Invariant A (No-live-reference-evict): an eviction commit must not occur while any batch owner holds a live reference to the slice.
- Invariant B (Prefix-consistency): for a prefixed request sequence, eviction+prefetch must preserve prefix semantics: cached prefix contexts must never be interleaved in a way that changes model output deterministically for the same prefix.
- Invariant C (Bounded-liveness): eviction decision must make forward progress within a bounded time for high-memory-pressure events (configurable emergency path).

Design details and data structures:
- Ledger: append-only ring buffer per-shard, small records for token state and owner lease registrations. Compact to avoid GPU-visible stalls.
- Token lifecycle: ALLOCATED -> PENDING (owner leases detected) -> READY -> COMMITTED -> RETIRED. Each transition is linearizable per-shard.
- Owner lease: lightweight timestamp + holder-id. Owners must renew on long-running batches. Renewal rate bounded to avoid thundering herd.
- Emergency reclaim path: if GPU memory falls below emergency threshold, the evictor can use a forced-demote that signals owners to copy KV slice to fallback memory (CPU pinned) with prioritized background transfer. This path requires explicit audit log entries and increases latency cost; used sparingly.

Test plan and validation harnesses:
- Unit tests: token lifecycle, ledger wrap-around, lease renewals, failure in middle of transition.
- Property tests: randomized sequences of allocations, prefetch, batch hold/release to assert Invariant A and B. Use proptest-style fuzz to discover edge races.
- Simulation: extend existing eviction fuzzer to simulate multi-tenant workloads, continuous batching, and varying kernel latencies. Include explicit failure-injection hooks (RPC loss, process pause, ledger truncation).
- Benchmarks: microbench for escrow overhead (token ops / ms) and end-to-end tail latency impact on typical chat workloads; stress test for reclaim throughput under memory pressure.

Monitoring and observability:
- Emit eviction-audit log shards to console tracing system. Dimensions: token_id, shard, epoch, lifecycle events, latency to commit, decision (commit/soft-defer/emergency-demote).
- New Console panels: token churn rate, average grace-window duration, emergency-reclaim frequency, prefix-collision incidents (where owner signaled blocking).

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): implement ledger + token allocation but keep evictor in no-op mode (only emit tokens). Run in prod for 2 weeks, collect telemetry and run verifier that replays proofs offline.
- Phase 2 (limited commit): enable commit for low-risk shards with low prefix density; monitor errors and tail latency for 1 week.
- Phase 3 (wide): enable across clusters with emergency path and telemetry alerts.

Acceptance criteria:
- No violation of Invariant A or B observed in extended simulation (100k randomized trials).
- Escrow token ops add <1% p99 token-op latency overhead in steady-state on benchmark hardware.
- Emergency reclaim path triggers audited and reduces GPU memory usage without data corruption in end-to-end tests.
- Console shows clear metrics and alerting rules for token churn and emergency reclaim rates.

Open questions / Trade-offs:
- Grace window sizing: default 50ms vs workload-specific tuning. Longer windows reduce false-positive evicts but increase memory pressure.
- Ledger footprint vs fidelity: smaller records minimize overhead but reduce offline-verifiability of prefix-histories.
- Forced-copy cost: copying hot KV slices to CPU memory introduces latency spikes; we may prefer soft demote + re-prefetch heuristics for typical workloads.

Security/Compliance notes:
- Eviction audit logs may include tenant IDs and prefix hints; ensure logs are redacted or routed to tenant-isolated telemetry when running in Dedicated/Private mode.
